eventMetadata.context_description: Latest National Weather Service guidance for Los Angeles International Airport (KLAX), the likely resolution station, projects a high near 65°F on May 4 amid persistent marine layer stratus clouds and moderate onshore winds around 5-10 mph, limiting solar heating in the LA basin. eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in Kuala Lumpur's equatorial climate, where May highs typically average 32–33°C amid inter-monsoon variability. Official Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) forecasts a maximum of 35°C on May 4 with isolated afternoon thunderstorms—potentially capping peaks via convective cloud cover and evaporative cooling—while global models like those on Weather.com project 33°C with 62% scattered thunderstorm risk. Differentiating factors include thunderstorm timing and coverage: limited activity could push toward 34–35°C as on May 1 (34°C actual), but widespread showers favor 31–32°C. Daily METMalaysia updates and model runs tomorrow will refine this, highlighting inherent short-term forecast divergence.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus favors 34°C at 36% implied probability for Jakarta's highest temperature on May 4, driven by recent observational data from BMKG stations showing late April peaks above 34°C (94°F on April 27) and a May 1 high near 33°C, amid the early onset of Indonesia's 2026 dry season that reduces cloud cover and convective activity for greater solar insolation. Historical early May averages cluster around 32°C, but Jakarta's urban heat island effect and BMKG's outlook for normal-to-slightly-warmer-than-normal temperatures (anomalies up to +0.6°C nationally) with normal rainfall support elevated outcomes like 33°C (25%) and 32°C (19%). Uncertainty persists from potential afternoon showers; monitor BMKG daily forecasts for updates on humidity and wind patterns influencing peak heating.
